beats.hook: I signed up for a store card at checkout and it quietly destroyed 11% of my available credit overnight.
beats.setup: I was 24, had a decent 680 credit score, and thought I was being smart building credit history. I had two existing cards with a combined $6,000 limit and almost no balances.
beats.mistake: The cashier said I'd save 20% on a $180 purchase, so I signed up on the spot. The store card came back with a $300 limit. That tiny limit meant even a $90 balance put me at 30% utilization on that card alone. My score dropped 34 points inside 60 days because of the hard inquiry plus that high utilization ratio hitting at the same time.
beats.fix: First, I paid that $90 balance completely within the next billing cycle. Then I called my existing card issuer and requested a credit limit increase, which bumped my total available credit from $6,300 to $9,300. I also set a $25 autopay on the store card so it always showed a tiny balance rather than zero or a spike.
beats.result: Within 5 months my score recovered to 694, and six months after that I was sitting at 711.
beats.cta: If this sounds familiar, drop your situation in the comments and I'll try to help.
